::: {#exr-rational-point-on-sphere} 
In classical geometry, we often parameterize curves using basic arithmetic. Use @exr-hypotenuse-calculation to determine a rational point on the Euclidean circle (a "1-face")
$$
    \Tb \coloneqq \{ (x,y) \in \Ab^2 \mid x^2 + y^2 = 1 \}.
$$
:::

::: {#exr-counting-faces}
Use @prp-cube-faces to answer the following.

(a) How many 3-dimensional faces does the unit 5-cube have?
(b) Show that a hypersquare $\Hsq{4}$ satisfies more coherence conditions than it has vertices (see @cor-coherence-count).
:::

:::: {.content-visible when-profile="instructor"}
::: {.solution}
(a) $\binom{5}{3} 2^{2} = 40$.

(b) By @cor-coherence-count, $\Hsq{4}$ satisfies $\binom{4}{2} 2^{2} = 24$ coherence conditions, while it has only $\binom{4}{0} 2^{4} = 16$ vertices.
:::
::::

> *Note*: Next week, we will see why this parameterization fails when $\Tb$ is replaced by the boundary of a 2-dimensional hypersquare!
